quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Is street racing legal?
questions.explanation: Street racing is illegal. It causes serious injuries and deaths. High speeds make it impossible for drivers to react to road hazards or other traffic situations.

questions.question: What does a green arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You may proceed, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if you also see a circular green light.
It shows the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may proceed, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may go. You must turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: What do orange signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn drivers about work zones. These signs are diamond-shaped with black letters or symbols. They warn that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: How can drivers prevent highway hypnosis?

options.text: Keep your eyes moving across the road instead of staring.
Drive no more than eight hours per day.

questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis is drowsiness from repeating sounds and low activity. To prevent it, move your eyes often, stop every 100 miles to stretch, and drive no more than eight hours in one day.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the other lane is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. A broken white line means you may cross it to pass if the lane ahead is clear.

questions.question: You should signal before turning. Signal at least ____ before you turn.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Use your turn signal or arm signal. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a roundabout?
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach a roundabout. Roundabouts are designed to be driven slowly.

questions.question: Which devices are not allowed on vehicles?
questions.explanation: Muffler cutouts are not allowed. Radar jamming devices that interfere with speed measurement tools are not allowed. Red lights and sirens are only allowed on emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A reduced speed zone is starting.
The reduced speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The reduced speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: The "End school zone" sign marks where the school zone speed limit ends. You can now drive at the normal speed limit.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: If you arrive at the same time as another vehicle to your right, yield to that vehicle. Wait until it is safe, then you may proceed.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: No one may pass from either direction.
Anyone may pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one may pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. You may only cross these lines to turn left or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, and scooter or skateboard riders when it is safe.

questions.question: Another person is injured in an accident with you. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them could make injuries worse. Keep them warm while waiting for help. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: When you drive faster, your tires work less well.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
When you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you drive faster, your tires work less well.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, faster speed makes your tires less effective. If you drive too fast, your tires lose grip on the wet surface and you may hydroplane, or slide on a layer of water.

questions.question: An eight-sided sign is always a:
questions.explanation: All eight-sided signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop at a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in a car's blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away they are or how fast they are going. Always watch carefully for motorcycles.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
Do not drive in this lane.
Left-turning traffic on a green light must wait for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left-turning traffic on a green light must wait for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way at a green light. You must wait for oncoming traffic to pass first.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Assume all other drivers will follow the rules.
Look for traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists before you go.
Wave other drivers forward before you move.
Go through the intersection right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists before you go.
questions.explanation: Even if you have the right-of-way, look both ways before entering the intersection. Check left, then right, then left again for traffic and bicyclists.

questions.question: What does a reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle mean?
questions.explanation: An orange triangle means the vehicle is moving slower than 25 mph. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When you approach an intersection with no traffic light or stop sign, you should:

options.text: Keep the same speed and continue.
Stop, check all directions, and then go.
Let all other drivers go first.

questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to stop by easing off the gas and covering the brake. Look left, right, then left again.

questions.question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, you should look:

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look at the right edge of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the headlights or you may be blinded for several seconds.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to make more distance between you.
Brake hard to force them to back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors several times a minute to spot tailgaters or fast-approaching cars. If a car is too close, slow down and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign says you cannot make a U-turn. Do not turn around where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the road mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic on the other side is going the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass, from either direction.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes:

options.text: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you will move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you will move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: To stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside them and do not tailgate them.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have large blind spots on the sides and back. Do not drive beside them and do not follow too closely behind them.

questions.question: When you face an oncoming car on the left and a bicycle on the right, you should:

options.text: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When there are multiple hazards, handle one at a time. If a bike is on the right and a car is coming toward you on the left, do not try to squeeze between both. Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and check for oncoming traffic.
Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.
When passing, wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.explanation: When passing, always signal at least 100 feet ahead. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Wait until you see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings and alert you to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a sharp turn is coming and you should reduce your speed.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Drives at the same speed always.
Only drives in places they know.

questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers can get distracted. A defensive driver watches what other drivers do and prepares for potential problems.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
If the pedestrian signals you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against the light or being careless.
